reviews.title: Jumping through hoops for “free”
reviews.text:
While it’s true that you don’t have to pay money to read, you are obligated to jump through hoops in the form of ads, subscriptions on multiple platforms, and commenting on every chapter you read in order to get tokens to read the next chapter. If you don’t want to have to read multiple stories and keep track of multiple plots at once, expect to be limited to reading a single chapter per day. 
Additionally you will find that there are no alpha readers or editors for the stories. No quality control to be found. Obvious spelling and grammar errors are rampant. I don’t even mean a missed comma or punctuation either: I mean errors that a very basic spelling check program would catch.
Finally, the stories are often written with exhausted and predictable tropes that flood the genre so heavily that a reader can grow disgusted by the characters and the story. Lack of communication,an instant physical attraction despite there being no personality traits that are attractive, mating bonds, rampant abuse and torture of a main character, toxic romances, etc.
Some stories are allowed to drag on unreasonably long, solely for the hits. Chapters are small, though supposedly several pages long in the app, barely made a single page in a writing program.
Not worth the effort.

reviews.title: Are the books worth the hassle?
reviews.text: So far the books I’ve tried have been promising, but I’m not sure if I’ll ever finish any of them. Each book I’ve tried started with several chapters with no strings. Then you get a few more if you are willing to watch about 3 minutes of ads for each. But, there is a limit on how many ads it will let you watch each day, and it doesn’t have the decency to even give you a countdown to renewed access. I can suffer the ads, but the cut off is ridiculous. I prefer reading one book at a time for hours at a time and this doesn’t make that feasible. The daily rewards are a joke, and I’m not willing to pay for any book that hasn’t had decent editing, and I have yet to find an app with that level of attention to grammar.

reviews.title: Exorbitant prices
reviews.text:
I downloaded this app for one story that’s not even complete because I’d seen an ad for it. After spending about an hour on the app, I can firmly say that this app is a scam for readers. There is a coin system in which each chapter of a book cost coins, of which the amount of coins go up each chapter, usually. You can watch about 3-4 minutes of ads between each individual chapter, which means you are only reading for about 3-4 minutes before another set of ads. Alternatively you can purchase coins. 
Doesn’t sound too bad right? You are paying to support an author right? Well, when was the last time you paid 60 dollars in coins to finish one not published,unfinished book? 
Because that’s how much it would have cost me to finish 183 chapters of an unfinished novel. And before you’re like ‘oh it must be a long novel’ *snort* I’ve picked up children’s books longer than it. 
This app takes advantage of readers and mostly like the authors as well. 
Do better, reading should be accessible to everyone. I wouldn’t be upset if it was around 5 dollars for a novel or 10-15 dollars a month for access to all work. Or even for the free version of ads supports spacing it every 5 or so chapters for a minute long. But currently? Unimpressed and disappointed.

reviews.title: Expensive & Frustrating
reviews.text:
I LOVE to read. And reading electronically doesn’t bother me as I use Apple Books for reading daily. This app is beyond expensive and frustrating…

Each chapter is broken up oddly into 6-9 phone-screen pages… about 2-3 book pages. The chapter breaks are at weird times as well… mid conversation, for example. Or they’re in a store shopping and it’ll be 2-3 “chapters” long. 

On top of that you have to pay for each of these chapters! They start out kind of reasonable at about 18 coins (coins are purchased with real money, but some can also be earned through ads and challenges/gifts), but once you’re hooked into the book they’re about 35-50 coins per “chapter”. I happened to check and it was almost 9,000 coins to read ONE book, at 299 “chapters” (about $40)!!! That’s astronomical!!! The normal price of a paperback book is anywhere from $7-15, so ~$40 is outrageous! And I don’t even know if I get forever access to the book!

If it weren’t for the good book I’m enjoying I would drop the app in a heartbeat, but I’ll finish it out for the sake of the book. 

This may be a “good” way for authors to get “published” initially, but for me who likes read all of an authors books when I like the writing style this is highly impractical at $40/book.
I did find this current author’s website and she mentions that she’s under contract with the big umbrella Corp for this app and can’t publish anywhere else until the contract ends. Big bummer!

reviews.title: I feel like I was scammed. I will not be giving this app more money.
reviews.text:
I was enjoying the story. Even purchased the 9.99 weekly pro pack that gave me 2500 coins. Plenty I thought to finish a book with 88 chapters. 

Not even close. So how it works. They lure you in with about 7 free chapters. Then a chapter cost 25 coins. You start to notice that coins go down by 1 coin for a dew chapters. It makes you think oh cool so as you read more they lower the coin cost. But then they say let’s do Auto Unlock. Now you never see the coins spent. And what you don’t realise is that then chapters range in coin cost from 40 to 60 coins. Your coins disappear quicker than you thought as the pattern was set prior to the unlock. 

I read WEBTOON and their coin system is fair. They are clear with each chapter cost. Chapter cost is the same for each chapter. This app and many more like it are just out to fleece you as they are not transparent nor consistent with cost of chapters and the UX is made difficult to navigate as they don’t want you exploring so that you understand what you are spending. 

Don’t be lured into the trap. And definitely don’t do Auto Unlock ! I am just going to renew my prime kindle monthly subscription for 9.99 and read all the romance there at a more reasonable cost that isn’t targeted to fleece you.
